distributionSurfaces.description: Vite application JavaScript, CSS, fonts, workers, and repository-owned WebAssembly deployed to Cloudflare Pages.
Versioned optional runtimes fetched from assets.soundscaper.org rather than bundled into Pages.
The desktop-specific Vite application copied into each Electron product; its composition excludes the Web FFmpeg wrapper and core runtime.

Translation and separately admitted runtime assets staged beside the Electron renderer, including exact reviewed libFLAC, libopus/libogg, libvorbis/libogg, WavPack, mpg123, LAME, and TwoLAME WebAssembly audio providers. Their runtime manifest authenticates each WASM file and its complete transitive JavaScript module closure before fresh supervised utility-process execution; application-supplied FFmpeg/libav, FFmpeg WebAssembly, and unqualified bundled WebM/AV1 payloads are excluded. Electron's separately inventoried alternate framework libffmpeg remains part of the Electron shell.

Electron, embedded Chromium and Node.js, Electron's exact alternate framework libffmpeg intended upstream to omit proprietary codec support, and the repository-owned main/preload process code. The framework library is not a Soundscaper codec-provider tier or patent-clearance evidence.

Public desktop packages, notices, checksums, and source archives required for content actually redistributed. Each package contains the seven exact reviewed compressed-audio WebAssembly providers and the exact verified Electron alternate framework libffmpeg for its target. Release assembly emits one preferred corresponding-source ZIP for those seven providers before SHA256SUMS: it fail-closed validates their exact shipped WASM identities, source manifests, upstream archives, Soundscaper wrappers, in-tree WavPack snapshot, build scripts and transitive helpers, configuration, relink instructions, and license texts, and records every included source byte in a deterministic internal receipt. This desktop source delivery does not close the separate Web FFmpeg corresponding-source or codec-patent gates. macOS ARM64 and Windows x64/ARM64 Soundscaper packages additionally require a target-native, canary-tested repository-owned operating-system codec addon whose exact manifest, payload, target, signing evidence, byte length, and SHA-256 are authenticated through staging and packaging; Linux has no OS codec payload and macOS x64 is unsupported. User-installed external FFmpeg remains outside this artifact closure and is not copied into the release set.

vendoredHeaders.rationale: The SPA format builders the native audio backend needs are static inline functions in the headers, so dlopen cannot reach them. Only headers are checked in; the library is resolved at runtime and never shipped.

releaseGates.qualification: A preferred deterministic corresponding-source ZIP is emitted and checksummed with every desktop release. It contains exact verified upstream source archives, the complete in-tree WavPack snapshot, Soundscaper wrappers, build scripts and transitive helpers, source configuration, relink/replacement instructions, and licenses for the seven exact shipped module identities. It does not qualify the separate Web FFmpeg runtime, Electron framework internals, OS providers, external FFmpeg, patent clearance, or non-infringement.

releaseGates.blocker: No versioned web route or web artifact currently delivers THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md with the deployed application and optional runtimes.
The current manifest identifies FFmpeg and ffmpeg.wasm archives but does not inventory and pin complete corresponding source for every enabled library in the binary.
No distribution-specific, jurisdiction-specific patent review is recorded for the enabled codec set.

futureDistributionGates.blocker: The current Utility Gain conformance package is repository-owned application code in the closed release catalog; it does not admit an externally authored or non-repository-owned package or satisfy that package's inventory, source, notice, and review duties.

Seven exact reviewed compressed-audio WebAssembly providers are admitted outside this future gate and execute in authenticated, isolated one-shot Electron utility processes: libFLAC, libopus/libogg, libvorbis/libogg, WavPack, mpg123, LAME, and TwoLAME. Specialized first-party PCM readers remain application code and libsndfile is not bundled. Windows Media Foundation and macOS ARM64 AudioToolbox use a target-native codec-only build for macOS ARM64, Windows x64, and Windows ARM64; the build runs native canaries, macOS signs before hashing, and staging, package, content-manifest, and startup checks bind one exact manifest and payload. Linux has no uniform OS tier and macOS x64 is unsupported. User-installed external FFmpeg has an exact live-qualified keyed-RGBA H.264/AAC MP4 and VP9/Opus WebM path, but those external bytes remain outside the production artifact closure. There is no admitted bundled or operating-system video provider and no libwebm, libvpx, dav1d, SVT-AV1, or libaom payload or complete five-target AV1 evidence, so bundled and operating-system WebM/AV1 execution fails closed. Electron's exact alternate framework libffmpeg is Chromium infrastructure rather than a provider tier, while user-installed external FFmpeg remains outside the production artifact closure.
